definition: Shakey the Robot was the first general-purpose mobile robot able to reason about its own actions.
details: While other robots would have to be instructed on each individual step of completing a larger task, Shakey could analyze commands and break them down into basic chunks by itself. Due to its nature, the project combined research in robotics, computer vision, and natural language processing. Because of this, it was the first project that melded logical reasoning and physical action. Shakey was developed at the Artificial Intelligence Center of Stanford Research Institute (now called SRI International). Some of the most notable results of the project include the A* search algorithm, the Hough transform, and the visibility graph method.

explainer.lead: Shakey the Robot was the first general-purpose mobile robot able to reason about its own actions, developed at the Artificial Intelligence Center of Stanford Research Institute (now SRI International). It matters because it was the first project to combine logical reasoning with physical action.

tiers.eli5: Unlike robots that had to be told every single step, Shakey could take a big command and figure out the small steps itself.
tiers.practitioner: Its design combined robotics, computer vision and natural language processing, so engineers treat it as an early example of decomposing a high-level command into executable actions. The pitfall it illustrates is that every component — perception, language, planning — must be correct for the whole task to work.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition applies; it is a historical system. Its known limits were those of its era: slow planning and perception constrained to simple, controlled environments.

explainer.example: Given a command to move an object, Shakey broke it into basic chunks itself rather than being instructed on each step.
